complex_k3_and_direct_obstructions.direct_conclusion: The direct full-NS rational branch is excluded by its proved dimension bound; its smooth-rational weak-log subcase was also excluded directly by the colouring calculation above.

outer_routing_verdict.consequence: Raw rationality, maximality, rank, cusp data, canonical colouring, MMP and section algebra do not force the proposed disjunction.  Therefore that disjunction cannot by itself prove the global n<=25 and finiteness theorem.
outer_routing_verdict.statement: There exists an absolutely reflection-maximal finite-volume arithmetic chamber which has neither a direct/RLogComp complex rational return nor a full-trace/projected-root complex-K3 return.

projective_plane_obstruction.conclusion: Neither of the two exhaustive adjunction colourings can occur on a complex rational surface; hence RLogComp is EMPTY for this raw P.

fano_subplane.conclusion: The Fano incidences force the three diagonal points to be collinear.  Their determinant is -2, so the configuration is representable only in characteristic 2, not over C.

projective_plane_obstruction.one_colouring: For t=1 the 21 pairing-minus-one short roots are disjoint (-1) curves and the 21 pairing-plus-one short roots are disjoint boundary (-4) curves; t=-1 exchanges the two parts.

rational_physical_square_class_exhaustio.principle: For one rational similarity c and a rational multiplier on each wall line, |C_i^2|/|r_i^2| has the common class [c] in Q*/Q*^2.

reflection_maximality.conclusion: The side group is absolutely maximal among discrete reflection overgroups, and hence maximal among arithmetic reflection groups.

esselmann_context_not_dependency.statement: Esselmann independently classifies the rank-22 endpoint as L and L* up to scale/isometry, but that classification is not used in the special-case overgroup proof above.

reflection_maximality.level_1_complete_root_chamber: Borcherds proves that the 210-wall polyhedron is a fundamental chamber for the full integral reflection group R(L).
reflection_maximality.level_2_arithmetic: R(L) has finite index in O^+(L), hence is a finite-covolume arithmetic reflection lattice.
level_3_classification_free_absolute_ove: If R(L) is contained in a discrete reflection group Gamma, then the lattice-overgroup index [Gamma:R(L)] is finite.
A finite extension of an arithmetic lattice is arithmetic.  Thus Gamma preserves some integral Lorentzian lattice M in the same rational commensurability class.
The 42 short simple reflections have connected odd Coxeter graph, so their root lines are one W-conjugacy class.  Rescale M so its intersection with every short-root line is Zr.
The short roots generate L integrally.  Hence L is contained in M.  For x in M, s_r(x)-x=(x,r)r belongs to M intersection Qr=Zr; therefore (x,L) is integral and M is contained in L*.
Intermediate lattices L <= M <= L* correspond to subgroups of A_L=(Z/2)^2.  The 210 wall reflections generate GL(2,F2)=S3 on A_L, whose only invariant subgroups are 0 and A_L.  Thus M is L or L*.
Dualization gives O(L)=O(L*) and therefore R(L)=R(L*).  Every generating reflection of Gamma preserves M, so Gamma is contained in R(M)=R(L).  The original inclusion forces equality.
